position: Office of the Secretary, Compliance for Grants and Other Federal Funding
proposal: The Mandate says FEMA and other DHS grants should go only to recipients that certify compliance with federal immigration law, including honoring detainers, and that they are registered with and use E-Verify (for states and localities, across all of government). State and local recipients would also commit to full information sharing with federal law enforcement and immigration authorities, including motor vehicle and voter registration databases. The text exempts post-disaster funding (and, as worded, nonhumanitarian funding) from these preconditions.
remaining: A certification covering E-Verify registration and use for all government components.
Data-sharing conditions covering motor vehicle and voter registration databases.
Conditions for FY2026 and later awards that survive the 2025 orders.

status_summary: EO 14159 (signed 2025-01-20, section 17) told the Attorney General and DHS to seek to stop federal funds going to jurisdictions that obstruct immigration enforcement, and EO 14287 (signed 2025-04-28) told agencies to identify funds to such jurisdictions for suspension or termination; DHS revised its standard grant terms on 2025-03-27 and 2025-04-18 to require state and local recipients to certify cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, including information sharing. On 2025-09-24 the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island (Illinois v. FEMA, No. 1:25-cv-00206) vacated those conditions and permanently enjoined their enforcement against the plaintiff states (20 states at filing, with the District of Columbia added in July 2025), on 2025-10-14 barred materially similar terms against them, and the government dismissed its appeal on 2026-09-16. FEMA applied FY2026 immigration conditions, including a detainer cooperation term, to nine grant programs by a bulletin of 2026-09-18, and on 2026-10-07 the plaintiff states asked the court to enforce its orders against them, citing nearly 1 billion dollars at risk, while a separate suit by other states over the FY2026 conditions (No. 26-cv-485) is pending. No requirement tied to E-Verify use or to motor vehicle and voter database access was found.

timeline.event: EO 14159 section 17 directed the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security to seek lawful steps to stop federal funds reaching jurisdictions that obstruct immigration enforcement.
DHS revised its standard grant terms to require state and local recipients to certify cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, including joint operations and information sharing.
EO 14287 directed publication of a list of sanctuary jurisdictions and had agencies identify federal funds to them for suspension or termination.
Twenty states sued FEMA and DHS in the District of Rhode Island over the immigration conditions (Illinois v. FEMA, No. 1:25-cv-00206).

The court granted summary judgment for the states, holding the six contested conditions arbitrary and capricious and a violation of the Spending Clause, vacated them and permanently enjoined their enforcement against the plaintiff states.
The court entered an order barring DHS and FEMA from enforcing the contested conditions or materially similar terms against the plaintiff states.
Defendants file a notice of appeal (ECF 78) to the First Circuit, No. 25-02131, per the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse docket summary.
The government voluntarily dismissed its appeal of the 2025 orders.

FEMA Information Bulletin No. 582 applies the FY2026 immigration-cooperation conditions to nine grant programs for awards issued on or after 2026-08-28, as described in the states' second motion to enforce.

The plaintiff states filed a second motion to enforce against eight DHS and FEMA fiscal year 2026 conditions, five identical to FY2025 terms and two modified, including added detail on detainer cooperation; the court had not ruled.

title: Condition FEMA and DHS grants on immigration compliance, E-Verify and data sharing
uncertainties: The 2025 DHS term changes are described by a trade publication and not by the DHS terms documents, which could not be opened; the FY2026 conditions and FEMA Information Bulletin No. 582 are described only in the states' motion, a party filing. The court orders of 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-14 were not read directly because the court docket host refuses fetches; their content comes from two party filings and a litigation tracker, which agree, and the appeal dismissal date comes only from the states' motion. Relief covers only the plaintiff states; whether the conditions are operative for other states was not confirmed beyond the pending separate suit. No Federal Register notice of the grant conditions was found. The Mandate's E-Verify and database-access certifications are broader than the cooperation conditions found. Stage is a judgment call: blocked reflects the vacatur and injunction for the plaintiff states and the dropped appeal, while the FY2026 terms show DHS continuing to issue similar conditions.
